newsitem.title: USA: Northrop Grumman to buy Logicon.
newsitem.headline: Northrop Grumman to buy Logicon.

text.p: Northrop Grumman Corp and Logicon Inc said they have signed a definitive merger agreement under which Logicon holders will get $52 worth of Northrop stock for each Logicon share they own.

Logicon stockholders will receive a fraction of a Northrop Grumman share determined by dividing $52 by the average closing price for Northrop Grumman common stock during a 30- day trading period prior to mailing the proxy statement in the merger.
In no event will the exchange ratio be more than 0.6919:1 or less than 0.5661:1.
Northrop Grumman said the merger will have a minimal impact on its 1997 earnings per share. The deal is subject to normal government reviews and shareholder approvals.

Upon completion of the deal, Northrop plans to form a new Logicon Information Technology Division that would combine substantial elements of Northrop's Data System and Services division and the operations of Logicon.

"This merger is consistent with our long-standing strategy to be a leader in the areas of surveillance, precision strike and advanced battle management," said Kent Kresa, Northrop Grumman chairman and chief executive.

"This merger will firmly establish Northrop Grumman as a key player in the defense information technology arena," Kresa said. "We see continued double-digit growth for this business area well into the next century.

Logicon chief executive Jack Woodhull said, "This merger will improve the business prospects of both companies, provide much broader resources for our customers and enhanced opportunities for our employees."
The new division, which will be led by Woodhull and headquartered in Torrance, Calif., will have revenues approaching $1 billion, the companies said.
Salomon Brothers acted as Northrop's financial advisor on the deal. Logicon was represented by Goldman Sachs.
